17 multiracial students enrolled at Blended Learning Academies Credit Recovery High School in 2024-25
17 multiracial students were enrolled at Blended Learning Academies Credit Recovery High School in the 2024-25 school year, a 240% increase from the previous year, according to the Michigan Department of Education.
Blended Learning Academies Credit Recovery High School enrolled 159 students during the 2024-25 school year. Multiracial students made up 10.7% of the student body, the third-largest group. White students were the largest group at 59.1% (94).
The school is part of the Blended Learning Academies Credit Recovery High School School District, whose central office is in Lansing.
Among the two schools in Blended Learning Academies Credit Recovery High School School District, Blended Learning Academies Credit Recovery High School recorded the highest enrollment of multiracial students in the 2024-25 school year.
In the 2025-26 school year, over 1.41 million students were enrolled in Michigan schools, a decline of about 5.3% from the nearly 1.45 million recorded before the pandemic in the 2019-20 school year. White student enrollment experienced the largest decline, falling about 5.8%.
